# Cleaning Laboratory Devices

Routine cleaning of laboratory devices reduces contamination risk and
extends device lifetime. This document covers the most common devices and
the recommended cleaning approach for each.

## General Principles

Cleaning agents must be compatible with the device material. Most plastic
housings tolerate isopropyl alcohol at moderate concentrations, but
prolonged exposure can degrade certain elastomers and seals. Always
consult the device manufacturer's documentation for the authoritative
recommendation; the guidance below is a starting point, not a
replacement.

Never spray cleaning agents directly onto a device. Apply the agent to a
lint-free wipe and use the wipe on the surface. This avoids fluid
ingress through vents and seams.

## Centrifuges

Wipe the rotor chamber after each session using a lint-free cloth
moistened with a 70 percent isopropyl alcohol solution. Remove the rotor
weekly for a more thorough clean. If a sample tube has broken inside
the chamber, follow the spill procedure in the decontamination guide
before any further use.

## Pipettes

Wipe the exterior of pipettes daily with 70 percent isopropyl alcohol.
The internal piston should be cleaned and re-greased quarterly. Do not
immerse a pipette in liquid; capillary action will draw fluid into the
mechanism.

## Microscopes

Objective lenses are cleaned with dedicated lens tissue and a small
amount of lens-cleaning solution. Never use isopropyl alcohol directly
on objective lenses, as it can damage the anti-reflective coating.
Eyepieces tolerate lens tissue with mild lens cleaner.

## Computer and Tablet Surfaces

For HP and similar laboratory computers, the manufacturer recommends a
70 percent isopropyl alcohol solution on a lint-free wipe. Higher
alcohol concentrations are not safer; they can cloud screens and damage
oleophobic coatings. Avoid bleach-based products on input surfaces.

## Recording the Clean

Each scheduled clean is logged in the Lab Operations Hub. Open the
device record, click "Log clean", and confirm the agent used and the
date. The log is reviewed during audits.
